With >=2 delegated restarts before first attest:ok the real core is token(1), yielding a false 'core-coupling' counterexample. Unexercised in boundary-01 (exactly one restart per order, attestation always refused) but contradicts the cited anchors. Unconditional equality violation contradicts stated conditional boundary: implement lines 140-142 append field='core==journal' whenever observed core!=journal, yet its own docstring (lines 17-22) states literal equality legitimately breaks after a first delegated attest:ok (core token(1), journal restart-serial) — reachable outside the two refused subclasses — producing a false 'counterexample' that double-reports the per-field-checked divergence. Related: an unbound collection/attestation sets first_break -> coupling_holds=False (lines 150-156) without appending a violation, so a corrupted case can yield status 'supported' while its own summary reports coupling_holds=False. Fix: gate the equality check on no delegated attest:ok observed, and promote first_break into violations/status.

No bounded-halt path and verdict conflation in control-build: charge.take(1) (line 89) is unguarded — a finite Counter raises mid-case and propagates through inspect_cases/run_controls, losing audited_prefixes and the counterexample-vs-budget distinction that implement handles via BudgetExceeded -> 'unproved' (lines 123-126). Restore/integrity failures return status 'counterexample' (lines 83-86), mislabeling evidence-binding faults as semantic counterexamples, and st[i] is indexed without the equal-length/side checks the checker performs (implement lines 111-115).
